relationships.description: The measurable end result is linked to a restriction on the solution space, such as a deadline or budget ceiling, that bounds how or by when the result may be achieved.
relationships.evidence: An outcome statement or decision record names the constraint explicitly, e.g. an OKR whose target date or cost cap cites the contractual deadline or budget policy.

relationships.description: The measurable end result is linked to the condition or pressure, such as a new regulation or rising cost, that motivated setting it.
relationships.evidence: The outcome's documentation or strategy deck cites the driver as its rationale, e.g. 'reduce hosting cost 20% by Q4' referencing the 'rising cloud spend' driver entry.

relationships.description: One measurable end result is related to another, for example as a prerequisite, sibling key result or complementary target under the same objective.
relationships.evidence: An OKR sheet or roadmap lists both key results under the same objective or states that one result's attainment depends on or accompanies the other.

relationships.description: The measurable end result is linked to the party whose interests it serves or who is accountable for tracking whether it is reached.
relationships.evidence: The outcome record names the stakeholder as owner or beneficiary, e.g. a KPI dashboard or OKR entry listing the product team or regulator role.

relationships.description: Achieving or missing the measurable end result positively or negatively affects progress toward the broader qualitative goal without fully realizing it.
relationships.evidence: Planning documents record a contribution or trade-off, e.g. a goal-tree annotation marking the outcome as '+' or '−' toward the goal.

relationships.description: The measurable end result is the concrete, checkable state whose attainment demonstrates that the qualitative goal has been reached.
relationships.evidence: An OKR or goal-refinement document lists the outcome as a key result of the goal, with its target value defining success for that goal.

relationships.description: Reaching the measurable end result is what actually delivers the benefit that stakeholders perceive as worthwhile.
relationships.evidence: A business case or value map states that the outcome's target, e.g. 'checkout under 2 minutes', produces the stated stakeholder value, e.g. 'saves customers ten minutes per order'.

notes: influence and realizes toward motivation.goal overlap; modelers should pick realizes for full attainment and influence for partial contribution. The associated-with links to constraint and driver are weak; constrained-by toward constraint and a driver→outcome influence would be more precise.
